title: Keep Linear/intake a short working board; leave the rest on qa/tickets
body:
Playtest visibility needs **two surfaces**, not one pile. The repo already meant this; a Grok wave showed the split leaking.

**Working board** — `intake/queue/` and its Linear AdventureForge mirror. Short. P0/P1 (and a rare P2). Things a person would start this week. `npm run work` reads only this. `docs/two_loop_workflow.md`: only `verified` / `corroborated` tickets cross into the queue; `accumulating` stays in the bucket.

**Idle shelf** — `qa/tickets/`. Everything triage extracted: accumulating, near-duplicates, taste, “we have seen this.” `npm run qa:bucket -- --summary` / `--all` / `--next` is how you look when the working board is quiet. An empty intake queue is normal; `loop.sh` then uses the assessor’s candidates (`report_qa_bucket` never fails the cycle).

The leak that would erase this split: `derivePromotion` (`src/qa/ticket.ts`) auto-corroborates any cluster whose evidence includes reference-tier, and `grok-4.6` is catalogued `reference` with `reasoning_effort: "low"` (`blind-tester/catalogs/grok_cli.json`). A 100-player grok-wave dry-run therefore marked **392 clusters corroborated**. Dumping those onto Linear is a fire alarm, not a board.

**Rule of thumb for a wave:** promote at most a small ranked set (about 3–7) into intake/Linear. Repeat mentions on an existing ticket become a comment, not a new issue. Do not auto-push every corroborated cluster.

Optional later: only P0/P1 ride `intake:sync:linear`; leave P2/P3 on the repo shelf. That is a follow-up, not a requirement to land this policy.
